# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Hypothesis title: Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy.

Hypothesis and context. In neuronal models of TDP-43 proteinopathy, a setting relevant to sporadic ALS with TDP-43 pathology, phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 is a required pore-intrinsic intermediate. The initiating event is persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing. Nup98 phosphorylation is proposed to keep nuclear import suppressed. Nuclear TDP-43 depletion, wider transport failure, and neuronal death are downstream responses. The claim is limited to this TDP-43 context and is not offered as a shared mechanism for every genetic ALS subtype.

Supported premises. Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components; disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems, and related pore pathology is present in ALS tissue [S1]. Those data support a TDP-43–pore connection and do not identify phosphorylation as the cause. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and impaired nuclear import, and transport-related manipulations modify phenotypes in that genetic context [S2]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form without conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and accompany import failure, loss of nuclear TDP-43, and cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in the assemblies [S3]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 is a different modification from nucleoporin phosphorylation. Separately, cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs nucleocytoplasmic transport, and changing stress-granule assembly modifies those defects [S4]. Read together, [S3] and [S4] separate a stress-granule sequestration route from a stress-granule-independent TDP-43 route. No supplied source shows that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS.

Speculative bridges. Nup98 as the relevant nucleoporin, any disease-associated phosphosites, and any kinase are assumptions. Unverified prior knowledge outside this packet is that FG-nucleoporins can be phosphorylated during mitosis or stress in non-ALS cells; that background does not establish the same events in ALS. The assumed bridge is that cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies lead a kinase to modify Nup98, that the modification alters FG-repeat interactions or NPC composition, and that this change sustains import blockade. No packet source demonstrates that interaction.

Alternatives. Transport factors may be sequestered in stress granules so import fails without a covalent pore change [S4]. TDP-43 aggregates may mislocalize nucleoporins directly, leaving phosphorylation as a bystander [S1]. In C9orf72 models, RanGAP mislocalization may explain import failure without Nup98 phosphorylation [S2]. Import failure may also be secondary to nonspecific cellular stress.

Discriminating preclinical test. Compare three arms in iPSC-derived motor neurons or primary rodent neurons: cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies induced while stress-granule assembly is suppressed; the same TDP-43 perturbation with stress granules intact; and a C9orf72 repeat-RNA model without engineered TDP-43 assemblies. Use time-resolved mass spectrometry of NPC fractions to order Nup98 phosphosites relative to cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, loss of nuclear TDP-43, and death. Replace endogenous Nup98 with a phospho-null or phospho-mimetic variant at mapped sites, at near-endogenous dosage, with total TDP-43 held constant. Readouts are NLS-reporter import, nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio, NPC composition, nucleoporin localization, RanGAP localization, stress-granule markers, and delayed neuronal death. The hypothesis predicts that in the stress-granule-suppressed TDP-43 arm, Nup98 phosphorylation follows assembly formation and precedes irreversible death; phospho-null Nup98 preserves import and nuclear TDP-43 despite persistent assemblies; and stress-granule suppression does not remove that phosphorylation-linked defect. In the C9orf72 arm, the same Nup98 genotypes should leave the RanGAP-linked import defect largely intact if the mechanism is context-specific. Temporal order plus these perturbations separates an initiating cytoplasmic TDP-43 event and a required Nup98 intermediate from a late correlate.

Falsifying observation. The hypothesis is falsified if mass spectrometry confirms that phospho-null Nup98 lacks the mapped modification and yet import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death proceed with unchanged kinetics and severity in the stress-granule-independent TDP-43 arm. Detection of Nup98 phosphorylation only after cell-death markers likewise marks it as a late correlate. Loss of both the transport defect and Nup98 phosphorylation as one package when stress granules are suppressed would favor sequestration [S4]. Absence of an import phenotype for both phospho-null and phospho-mimetic Nup98 would falsify a functional role for the mapped sites.

Limitations. Kinase and site identity must be measured. Redundant phosphorylation of other nucleoporins can produce a false-negative single-gene result. Phospho-mimetic substitutions miss kinase timing and localization. Cultured neurons compress a years-long human disease, and TDP-43-model results do not automatically transfer to C9orf72 or SOD1 ALS. The design tests necessity and order in preclinical systems; it does not validate a therapy.

Ranked proposal:
Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy
